articles.title: Cerebral Cavernous Malformation Mimicking a Transient Ischemic Attack: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: A cerebral cavernous malformation can mimic a transient ischemic attack. Recurrent, brief, stereotyped episodes with unilateral facial twitching and sensory symptoms should raise suspicion for focal seizures. Brain MRI with susceptibility-sensitive sequences can help identify an underlying cavernous malformation.

articles.title: Changes in the functional outcomes of surgical resection of unruptured cerebral arteriovenous malformations after the year 2015: from 556 patients of the nation-wide, real-world database in Japan.
articles.abstract: The benefits of surgical resection of unruptured cerebral arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) remains controversial. In 2014, The ARUBA (A Randomized trial of Unruptured Brain Arteriovenous Malformations) trial reported worse outcomes with the interventional treatment strategies used in the trial than with medical management alone. In parallel, patient selection, choice of multimodalities, and perioperative management, for safe and effective AVM treatment, have recently developed. Thus, whether the proportion of functional deterioration following surgical resection has decreased over time is of particular interest. The present study aimed to investigate the yearly trends in the functional outcomes of surgical resection of unruptured AVMs using data from a nationwide payment system-linked database in Japan. A total of 556 surgeries were analyzed. Yearly trends of functional deterioration defined as deterioration to postoperative modified Rankin Scale 2 or more at discharge, use of preoperative embolization, and perioperative complications, were investigated by interrupted time-series and multivariable mixed-effects logistic regression analyses. Functional deterioration was observed in 70/556 (12.6%) patients. The proportion of functional deterioration in the year 2015-2019 was significantly lower than that in the year 2011-2014 (28/297 [9.4%] vs. 42/259 [16.2%], adjusted odds ratio: 0.51, 95% confidence interval: 0.28-0.93, p = 0.027) by mixed-effects logistic regression analysis. The significant level change in the decreasing trend of the functional deterioration in 2015 might indicate the ARUBA trial prompted more conservative selection of patients for surgery, although this interpretation remains speculative due to lack of information on angioarchitecture and patient selection.

articles.title: A novel non-contrast-enhanced MRA using silent scan for evaluation of brain arteriovenous malformation: A case report and review of literature.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Brain arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) are congenital vascular abnormalities involving abnormal connections between arteries and veins. In clinical practice, imaging studies help evaluate feeding arteries, niduses, draining venous systems, and coexisting complications in patients with brain AVM. They also have an impact on decision-making regarding clinical management. We applied a novel non-contrast-enhanced MR angiography (MRA) technique, termed "silent MRA," for evaluating an incidental brain AVM. Here, we describe the clinical case with radiological review and highlight the technical background and clinical usefulness of silent MRA.
PATIENT CONCERNS: A 60-year-old woman underwent neuroimaging study including MRA to evaluate intracranial cause of headache.
DIAGNOSES: The brain AVM, including its nidus and draining veins, was conspicuously delineated on silent MRA images; these findings correlated well with conventional angiographic findings.
INTERVENTIONS: The patient did not receive interventional or surgical treatment.
OUTCOMES: The patient is being followed up regularly at the outpatient department.
LESSONS: The silent MRA can be a suitable imaging modality for repeated follow-up evaluation for not only brain AVMs but also various intracranial vascular diseases without the use of contrast materials.

articles.title: Linking Brain Arteriovenous Malformations With Anorectal Hemorrhoids: A Clinical and Anatomical Review.
articles.abstract: Patients who harbor brain arteriovenous malformations are at risk for intracranial hemorrhage. These malformations are often seen in inherited vascular diseases such as hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia. However, malformations within the brain also sporadically occur without a hereditary-coding component. Here, we review recent insights into the pathophysiology of arteriovenous malformations, in particular, certain signaling pathways that might underlie endothelial cell pathology. To better interpret the origins, determinants and consequences of brain arteriovenous malformations, we present a clinical case to illustrate the phenotypic landscape of the disease. We also propose that brain arteriovenous malformations might share certain signaling dimensions with those of anorectal hemorrhoids. This working hypothesis provides casual anchors from which to understand vascular diseases characterized by arteriovenous lesions with a hemorrhagic- or bleeding-risk component. articles.title: Functional impairments for outcomes in a randomized trial of unruptured brain AVMs.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the effects of medical vs interventional management on functional outcome in A Randomized Trial of Unruptured Brain Arteriovenous Malformations (ARUBA).
METHODS: We used the initial results of a nonblinded, randomized, controlled, parallel-group trial involving adults ≥18 years of age with an unruptured brain arteriovenous malformation (AVM) to compare the effects of medical management (MM) with or without interventional therapy (IT) on functional impairment, defined by a primary outcome of death or symptomatic stroke causing modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score ≥2. ARUBA closed recruitment on April 15, 2013.
RESULTS: After a median of 33.3 months of follow-up (interquartile range 16.3-49.8 months), of the 223 enrolled in the trial, those in the MM arm were less likely to experience primary outcomes with an mRS score ≥2 than those who underwent IT. The results applied for both those as randomized (MM n = 109 vs IT n = 114) (hazard ratio [HR] 0.25, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.11-0.57, p = 0.001) and as treated (MM n = 125 vs IT n = 98) (HR 0.10, 95% CI 0.04-0.28, p < 0.001). Functional impairment for the outcomes showed no significant difference by Spetzler-Martin grade for MM but was more frequent with increasing grades for IT (p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Death or stroke with functional impairment in ARUBA after a median follow-up of 33 months was significantly lower for those in the MM arm both as randomized and as treated compared with those with IT. Functional severity of outcomes was lower in the MM arm, regardless of Spetzler-Martin grades.
CLINICALTRIALSGOV IDENTIFIER: NCT00389181.
CLASSIFICATION OF EVIDENCE: This study provides Class II evidence that for adults with unruptured brain AVMs, interventional management compared to MM increases the risk of disability and death over ≈3 years.

articles.title: Aberrant Artery Contributing to Thoracic Outlet Syndrome.
articles.abstract: Thoracic outlet syndrome results from the compression of neurovascular structures as they pass through the thoracic outlet, often leading to neurogenic symptoms involving the brachial plexus. We present two cases of young adults with persistent upper arm and hand symptoms due to brachial plexus compression associated with aberrant arteries. Despite nonsurgical management, including physical therapy and anti-inflammatory medications, both patients continued to experience disabling symptoms. Surgical exploration has revealed previously undescribed anomalous arterial branches deep to the anterior scalene muscle and crossing directly over the C7-T1 nerve roots. These arteries were ligated and divided, in addition to brachial plexus neurolysis and scalenectomies. Both patients experienced complete resolution of symptoms postoperatively and returned to full activity. Given that the vascular anomaly was addressed alongside standard decompression procedures, its independent contribution to symptom relief cannot be fully established. However, the direct relationship between the aberrant artery and compressed nerve roots suggests it remains a contributing factor. These cases highlight the importance of considering rare vascular anomalies as potential contributors to neurogenic thoracic outlet syndrome, particularly in the young adult population. Recognition of such variants is critical during surgical dissection, as standard imaging may not identify these atypical compressive structures.

articles.title: Retrospective cohort analysis of spontaneous regression in pediatric lymphatic malformations and its role in modern multidisciplinary approach.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lymphatic malformations (LMs) often require active treatment, including sclerotherapy, surgery, or sirolimus. However, some lesions regress spontaneously, and factors associated with spontaneous regression remain incompletely undefined. In this study, we aimed to investigate the incidence, timing, and predictors of spontaneous regression in pediatric LMs.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 118 patients diagnosed with LMs before 20 years of age and by 2025 who had documented outpatient follow-up and/or treatment at our institution between January 2007 and April 2026. Spontaneous regression was defined as a >50% reduction in lesion volume without standard LMs-directed treatment, with no clinically significant symptoms, only minimal residual cosmetic concern, and no active treatment considered necessary; regression was confirmed by MRI in all cases. Logistic regression was performed to identify associated factors. Cumulative incidence of spontaneous regression was estimated using a competing-risks approach, with initiation of LMs-directed treatment before regression as a competing event.
RESULTS: Spontaneous regression occurred in 43 of 118 patients (36.4%), including 33 of 59 macrocystic lesions (55.9%) versus 10 of 59 non-macrocystic lesions (16.9%). Macrocystic morphology remained significantly associated with regression after multivariable adjustment (odds ratio, 5.11; 95% confidence interval, 1.94-13.45; p < 0.001). The cumulative incidence of spontaneous regression was 26.6% (95% CI, 18.5-34.7%) at 1 year, 31.1% (22.6-39.6%) at 2 years, and 35.9% (27.0-44.8%) at 5 years. Among regressors, the median time to documented regression was 193 days (range, 5-2869 days).
CONCLUSIONS: Spontaneous regression occurred in a substantial proportion of pediatric LMs and was strongly associated with macrocystic morphology. Careful initial observation may be a reasonable management strategy for selected clinically stable patients within a multidisciplinary approach.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level II Retrospective Study.

articles.title: Mural Cell Dysfunction and Therapeutic Strategies in Extracranial Arteriovenous Malformations.
articles.abstract: Extracranial arteriovenous malformations (eAVMs) are congenital high-flow vascular anomalies characterized by direct connections between arteries and veins, resulting in progressive lesion growth, recurrent bleeding, pain, and significant morbidity. Recent studies suggest that somatic mutations in endothelial cells (ECs), most commonly in MAP2K1 and KRAS, initiate eAVM formation. However, these mutations alone cannot fully explain the abnormal vascular architecture, vessel instability, or frequent recurrence after treatment. Mural cells (MCs), including pericytes (PCs) and vascular smooth muscle cells (vSMCs), may also contribute to eAVM progression, although their role remains unclear. Under normal conditions, ECs and MCs communicate through signaling pathways such as PDGFB-PDGFRβ, Ang1-Tie2, Notch3, and TGF-β to regulate MC recruitment, vessel maturation, barrier integrity, vascular tone, and extracellular matrix homeostasis. In eAVMs, changes in these signaling pathways may affect MC recruitment and function, contribute to changes in vSMC phenotype, and influence vascular stability. However, these mechanisms have not been fully established in human eAVMs. This review summarizes the physiological roles of MCs in vascular homeostasis, discusses the possible mechanisms responsible for MC dysfunction in eAVMs, and reviews current procedural and targeted medical therapies and their effects on the EC-MC unit. Emerging therapeutic strategies aimed at restoring EC-MC communication and vascular stability are also reviewed. The possible contribution of MCs to eAVM pathogenesis provides a broader view of disease biology. However, whether therapies targeting both EC abnormalities and MC dysfunction can improve long-term vascular stability and reduce lesion recurrence remains to be determined.

articles.title: Advances in the management of myasthenia gravis.
articles.abstract: Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder of the neuromuscular junction characterised by fluctuating fatigable weakness of skeletal muscles. Advances have led to the identification of distinct antibody subtypes and expanding therapeutic options, transforming myasthenia gravis from a disease of significant morbidity and mortality to one that is increasingly manageable. This review presents a comprehensive overview of myasthenia gravis, including its epidemiology, pathogenesis, classification, diagnostic strategies, and treatment modalities. Established therapies are discussed, including acetylcholinesterase inhibitors, corticosteroids, conventional oral immunosuppressants, intravenous immunoglobulin, plasma exchange, B cell depleting agents, complement inhibitors, neonatal fragment crystallisable receptor inhibitors, and thymectomy. A dedicated section highlights emerging treatments. Special considerations for pregnancy, myasthenic crisis, and individualised treatment approaches are emphasised. Physician-patient communication is highlighted as a critical factor in optimising adherence and outcomes. Effective integration of novel therapies into clinical practice depends on a clear understanding of their mechanisms, safety profiles, and applicability across diverse patient populations. As therapeutic complexity increases, improved clinical outcomes will require continued refinement of clinical tools, treatment algorithms, optimal communication strategies, and robust data to guide evidence based decision making.

articles.title: Pushing the boundaries in extending cardiac graft preservation: Hypothermic, oxygenated perfusion (HOPE) versus enhanced normothermic perfusion in a porcine model of donation after circulatory death (DCD).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Excellent outcomes have been reported for heart transplantation with donation after circulatory death (DCD) using graft preservation/evaluation protocols with normothermic ex situ heart perfusion (ESHP); however, little information is available for hypothermic oxygenated perfusion (HOPE). We investigated extending heart preservation with HOPE versus normothermic perfusion (NP) enhanced with plasma exchange using a porcine DCD model.
METHODS: Healthy male adult pigs underwent simulated DCD with 15 minutes of warm ischemia. Two ESHP groups were included: enhanced NP (continued as long as ventricular contraction/coronary perfusion was maintained) versus HOPE (20 hours pre-defined duration). Cardiac recovery was evaluated in all hearts under normothermic conditions with ex situ left-ventricular loading.
RESULTS: ESHP was significantly longer in HOPE versus NP hearts (23.5 versus 10.5 hours, p<0.05), while ventricular, vascular and metabolic recovery remained similar. Markers of oxidative stress and myocardial cell death, as well as cytokine release, were significantly reduced with HOPE compared to NP, but increased upon rewarming to levels similar to NP hearts.
CONCLUSION: Both enhanced NP and HOPE enable extended ESHP of DCD hearts. Although HOPE preservation provides several benefits, such as ESHP times beyond 20 hours and cardioprotection by lowering oxidative stress and inflammation, the transition from HOPE to normothermic conditions poses a risk of rewarming-related damage, and graft evaluation methods during HOPE remain to be developed. Further research towards the optimization of HOPE for DCD hearts is required.

articles.title: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura -treatment standard.
articles.abstract: We review the current standards of treatment and discuss novel developments in the pathophysiology, diagnosis, outcome prediction and management of thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP). TTP results from a severe deficiency of the metalloprotease enzyme, ADAMTS13, normally required for the cleavage of von Willebrand factor (vWF) into haemostatically active multimers. Increased platelet binding to these large and ultra large vWF multimers, results in microthrombi release in the microcirculation, resulting in TTP symptoms and potential end-organ damage. There are 2 types of TTP: immune-mediated (iTTP), constituting the majority of cases, and congenital (cTTP), accounting for 5-10% of all presentations. TTP is a medical emergency and initiation of therapy is paramount to improve outcomes. Plasma exchange (PEX) replaces ADAMTS13 and removes IgG auto-antibodies to ADAMTS13. Caplacizumab is given on confirmation of acute TTP. It prevents binding between platelets' GP1b receptors and the A1 domain of vWF, accelerating platelet count recovery, reducing PEX duration and preventing exacerbations and refractory disease. Finally, immunosuppressive therapy, principly with steroids and rituximab are started in the acute TTP setting. Long term follow-up of TTP is required, during which a reduction in ADAMTS13 activity to 15-20 IU/dL (%) necessitates elective rituximab treatment to normalise ADAMTS13 activity level and prevent a clinical relapse. cTTP requires ADAMTS13 replacement, until recently this was with fresh frozen plasma or intermediate factor VIII concentrates. However, recombinant ADAMTS13 provides superior outcomes in relation to reductions in acute and subacute TTP and non-overt symptoms. Treatment should be at least every 2 weeks.

articles.title: Autoimmune Cerebellar Degeneration Caused by Septin-7 and Septin-5 Antibodies: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Septin antibodies represent rare targets in autoimmune cerebellar ataxia, with limited data on optimal therapeutic strategies. We report a case of dual septin-5 and septin-7 positive autoimmune cerebellar degeneration with detailed long-term treatment outcomes. A 42-year-old previously healthy Caucasian male developed acute-onset progressive cerebellar ataxia with multidirectional nystagmus. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis revealed lymphocytic pleocytosis, oligoclonal bands, and positive septin-7 antibodies; subsequent testing confirmed dual positivity for septin-5 antibodies. Initial treatment with intravenous methylprednisolone, plasma exchange, and intravenous immunoglobulin showed minimal improvement. MRI showed subsequent cerebellar atrophy, and there was decline in motor strength with progression to wheelchair use. Aggressive immunosuppression with cyclophosphamide achieved disease stabilization and stabilization in cerebellar atrophy progression. Transition to rituximab maintenance therapy was associated with continued clinical and radiological stability and modest functional improvements over 18 months of follow-up. This case demonstrates that the use of cyclophosphamide followed by rituximab maintenance represents a viable strategy for dual septin-positive autoimmune cerebellar degeneration.

articles.title: Probable Propylthiouracil-Associated Thrombotic Microangiopathy With Dialysis-Requiring Acute Kidney Injury and Proteinase 3-Antineutrophil Cytoplasmic Antibody Positivity: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Propylthiouracil (PTU) is a recognised cause of hepatotoxicity and drug-induced antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA) positivity, but thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA) attributed to PTU is rarely reported. We describe a 27-year-old woman with refractory Graves' disease who had received escalating doses of PTU for at least eight months, reaching 200 mg twice daily. She presented with vomiting and jaundice and was found to have microangiopathic haemolytic anaemia (lactate dehydrogenase 4,901 U/L, undetectable haptoglobin, and red cell fragments), a platelet count of 19-28 × 10⁹/L, bilirubin of 322 µmol/L, alanine aminotransferase of 447 U/L, and oligoanuric acute kidney injury (creatinine 617-856 µmol/L from a baseline of 38-46 µmol/L). ADAMTS-13 (a disintegrin and metalloproteinase with a thrombospondin type 1 motif, member 13) activity was 53.4 IU/dL, excluding thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura. PTU was stopped on admission on 14 December 2025. Proteinase 3 (PR3)-ANCA was positive at 78.7 chemiluminescent units (CU) (reference <20), so she received high-dose prednisolone, three sessions of plasma exchange, and rituximab 1 g before a native renal biopsy. She required four haemodialysis sessions. Fibrinogen fell from 4.18 to 0.40 g/L with albumin-based exchange and was 1.38 g/L on the day of biopsy despite cryoprecipitate. Biopsy showed severe glomerular TMA with early cortical necrosis, negative immunofluorescence, no electron-dense deposits, and no vasculitis, and was complicated by perinephric haemorrhage requiring interlobar artery embolisation. Eculizumab was started pending complement studies and stopped after four weeks when no pathogenic complement variant or factor H autoantibody was found. There was no relapse after withdrawal. She underwent total thyroidectomy and became dialysis-independent. At nine months, the estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) had stabilised at 55-63 mL/min/1.73 m² with persistent proteinuria (protein:creatinine ratio 61-79 mg/mmol) on ramipril. This case shows that PTU should be considered a cause of TMA, that ANCA positivity in PTU-treated patients needs histological confirmation, that fibrinogen should be checked before biopsy after plasma exchange, and that survivors need long-term kidney follow-up.

articles.title: Therapeutic Plasma Exchange Use among ANCA-Associated Vasculitis Hospitalizations after PEXIVAS and Guidelines, 2016-2023.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE) has historically been considered for antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis (AAV) with severe kidney or pulmonary involvement. National inpatient use after publication of the Plasma Exchange in Vasculitis (PEXIVAS) trial remains incompletely characterized.
METHODS: We conducted a repeated cross-sectional analysis of adult National Inpatient Sample hospitalizations from 2016 through 2023. The primary AAV cohort used stable International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) codes. We estimated survey-weighted annual and era-specific TPE use and age- and sex-adjusted era associations. Lupus nephritis (LN) served as a temporal comparator in an adjusted cohort-by-era model. Sensitivity analyses examined principal-diagnosis AAV, AKI, AKI requiring acute kidney replacement therapy (AKI-D), coded pulmonary hemorrhage, and length of stay greater than 1 day.
RESULTS: The cohort included 20,866 AAV hospitalizations and 623 TPE events. Weighted TPE use declined from 4% in 2016-2019 to 2% in 2022-2023; the adjusted later-versus-baseline odds ratio (OR) was 0.49 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.39-0.62). Standardized TPE probabilities declined from 3.81% to 1.91% for AAV and from 1.04% to 0.68% for LN. The absolute difference-in-changes was -1.54 percentage points (95% CI, -2.15 to -0.94), whereas the interaction OR was 0.75 (95% CI, 0.52-1.10; P = 0.14). Baseline-to-later TPE use declined from 14% to 7% in principal-diagnosis AAV, 35% to 14% in AKI-D, and 32% to 23% with coded pulmonary hemorrhage. The length-of-stay-greater-than-1-day result was similar to the primary analysis.
CONCLUSIONS: Inpatient TPE use among U.S. AAV hospitalizations declined during 2016-2023, including in multiple coded clinical-context sensitivities. The decline aligned with evolving trial evidence and guidelines, although these data cannot establish causation or appropriateness of treatment decisions.

articles.title: A Rare Autoantibody with Catastrophic Consequences.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Anti-melanoma differentiation-associated protein 5 (MDA5)-positive dermatomyositis is an uncommon inflammatory myopathy associated with minimal muscle involvement, rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease, and high mortality (1). We describe a severe case with rapidly progressive multisystem involvement requiring aggressive multimodal immunosuppression.
METHOD: A clinical case presentation with targeted literature review.
RESULTS: A previously well 40-year-old woman from Kenya presented with several weeks of cough, fatigue, weight loss, and progressive rash. Examination demonstrated heliotrope rash, Gottron papules, and severe digital pulp ischaemia with evolving dry gangrene. Laboratory testing showed anti-MDA5 and anti-Ro52 antibodies, elevated creatine kinase and transaminases, and thrombocytopenia. Magnetic resonance imaging of the thighs demonstrated bilateral symmetrical myositis, while chest imaging showed basal ground-glass pulmonary changes. Her course was complicated by spontaneous bilateral psoas muscle haematomas causing left femoral nerve palsy, recurrent seizures requiring intensive care admission, and neuropsychiatric symptoms. Her treatment included high-dose corticosteroids, intravenous immunoglobulin, rituximab, and tofacitinib, with subsequent escalation to cyclophosphamide and plasma exchange. Following prolonged inpatient care, she survived the acute illness and underwent rehabilitation with gradual improvement in left lower limb strength.
CONCLUSION: MDA5-positive dermatomyositis can follow a catastrophic course with rare multisystem complications. In severe or refractory disease, rapid recognition and early aggressive multimodal immunosuppression are critical to maximising the chance of meaningful recovery.

articles.title: JAK Inhibition in Febrile Infection-Related Epilepsy Syndrome: A Case Series from Sydney Children's Hospital.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Febrile Infection-Related Epilepsy Syndrome (FIRES) is a subcategory of New-Onset Refractory Status Epilepticus (NORSE) occurring in previously healthy individuals following a mild febrile illness. FIRES is a challenging paediatric condition with a mortality of 12% and permanent neurocognitive deficits in up to 90% of survivors. Pathogenesis appears to involve innate immune dysregulation, and first-line immunotherapy (intravenous immunoglobulin [IVIG], corticosteroids) is ineffective in most cases. A number of second-line cytokine-directed therapies have been trialled in individual case reports and short case series, but with similarly unencouraging outcomes.
METHOD: We describe three paediatric patients managed at Sydney Children's Hospital between 2024 and 2026 in whom baricitinib, a JAK1/2 inhibitor, was incorporated into the immunotherapy regimen for FIRES.
RESULTS: Patient 1 was a 13-year-old girl diagnosed with FIRES with refractory status epilepticus. After 2 months of uncontrolled seizures with profound functional decline and brain atrophy, baricitinib was added to her treatment regimen. While she eventually succumbed to her illness, the introduction of JAK inhibition was accompanied by electroencephalogram (EEG) normalisation within two weeks. Patient 2, a 15-year-old girl, presented following a post-appendicectomy febrile illness. She developed refractory status epilepticus with negative autoimmune and paraneoplastic workup and markedly elevated neopterin (347 nmol/L; normal range [NR] = 0 - 30). Treatment with IVIG, methylprednisolone, and plasma exchange (PLEX) followed by baricitinib and anakinra achieved seizure control over a period of weeks. Intermittent focal seizures and encephalopathic EEG changes persist, but with return to premorbid function and return to school. Patient 3 is a 16-year-old girl who presented in March 2026 with febrile encephalopathy and escalating seizures. Following intubation, multi-agent antiepileptic therapy, and immunosuppression, including baricitinib, anakinra, and IVIG, she was extubated after 2 weeks with subsequent functional recovery, returning to school with mild residual cognitive and emotional changes.
CONCLUSION: This case series adds to the limited evidence supporting early and aggressive JAK inhibition in paediatric FIRES. The addition of baricitinib appears to offer clinically meaningful seizure reduction and EEG improvement when used alongside cytokine-directed therapy.

articles.title: [A successful treatment case of repeated oral large-dose colchicine poisoning].
articles.abstract: Colchicine poisoning is correlated with high mortality and disability rates, due to its narrow therapeutic window, high toxicity, lack of specific early clinical manifestations, no specific detoxification drugs, and potential to trigger multiple organ dysfunction. We reported a case of acute poisoning caused by repeated self-administration of large-doses of colchicine at the Department of Emergency Medicine of the First Affiliated Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University. The patient was admitted to the hospital three times in 2020, 2023, and 2024. Following colchicine ingestion, the patient presented with clinical symptoms such as shock, multiple organ dysfunction syndrome (MODS), and hepatorenal insufficiency. After underwent gastric lavage, catharsis, intermittent plasma exchange (PE) combined with continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT), and organ support treatment, the patient's condition improved, and eventually recovered and was discharged from the hospital.

articles.title: [Successful treatment of a case of acute arsine poisoning via plasma exchange].
articles.abstract: Acute arsine poisoning manifests with an abrupt onset and is characterized by core clinical features including acute intravascular hemolysis, renal injury, and multi-organ dysfunction, accompanied by a high mortality rate. On July 26, 2024, the Tianjin Occupational Disease Prevention and Therapeutic Hospital admitted a 37-year-old male patient who had inhaled arsine gas for approximately 2 minutes and subsequently developed abdominal pain, cola-colored urine, and scleral and cutaneous jaundice. At admission, the patient's hemoglobin level was 103 g/L and his urinary arsenic concentration was 0.545 mg/L. Based on the patient's history of exposure to the toxic substance and his clinical presentation, he was diagnosed with acute severe arsine poisoning. Upon admission, the patient received immediate intensive therapy consisting of plasma exchange (PE) combined with glucocorticoids, urinary alkalinization, and organ support. On day 3 after PE, the patient's urine color cleared; by day 5, his serum total bilirubin level had decreased to 32.9 μmol/L; and by day 14, his urinary arsenic concentration had dropped to 0.064 mg/L. The patient was fully recovered and discharged; follow-up examinations at 3 months revealed no abnormalities in renal function. This case demonstrates that early implementation of intensive therapy centered on plasma exchange can effectively eliminate toxic substances from the body, halt the progression of hemolysis, and protect renal function, thereby holding clinical significance for improving the success rate of emergency treatment in acute severe arsine poisoning.

articles.title: Anti-TREM2 antibody VHB937 binds IgSF domain to reduce microglial inflammation in preclinical and clinical studies.
articles.abstract: TREM2 is a lipid-binding receptor expressed in the brain in microglia. Activation of TREM2 is critical for microglia to adopt a disease-associated phenotype. Here we describe VHB937, a human antibody that activates TREM2 by binding to the IgSF domain. In vitro in human iPS-derived microglia, VHB937 expands a phagocytic subcluster at the expense of a pro-inflammatory subcluster, facilitates chemotaxis and phagocytosis, and reduces the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines like SPP1. In vivo, VHB937 reduces degeneration of dopaminergic neurons in the MPTP model and accelerates re-myelination in the cuprizone model. Chronic treatment in a mouse amyloidosis and tauopathy model results in reduction of dystrophic neurites with no effect on plaque load and of pathogenic tau species, respectively. We further show in a first-in-human clinical trial that VHB937 engages TREM2 based on reduction of SPP1 in CSF. We conclude that VHB937 has the potential to change microglial state toward a neuroprotective phenotype, offering therapeutic potential for neurodegenerative/neuroinflammatory disorders.

articles.title: Giant-Cell Arteritis.
articles.abstract: Giant-cell arteritis is a granulomatous vasculitis of large and medium-sized arteries that occurs almost exclusively in older adults. Suspected giant-cell arteritis warrants urgent diagnostic evaluation and, when ischemic risk is high, immediate treatment before diagnostic confirmation. Although glucocorticoids remain the cornerstone of therapy, treatment is frequently prolonged, associated with substantial toxic effects, and complicated by relapses. Advances in vascular imaging and insights into disease immunopathogenesis have expanded our understanding of disease heterogeneity and enabled the development of targeted therapies, particularly interleukin-6-receptor and Janus kinase inhibitors. Here, we review current concepts in the pathogenesis, clinical presentation, diagnosis, and management of giant-cell arteritis and highlight areas of uncertainty that warrant further investigation.

articles.title: Recent advances in the glioma tumor microenvironment (TME): cellular interactions, signaling networks, and therapeutic opportunities.
articles.abstract: Gliomas are treatment-resistant primary brain tumors, with glioblastoma (GBM) representing the most aggressive adult-type diffuse glioma. Their progression reflects the interplay between tumor-intrinsic alterations and the surrounding tumor microenvironment (TME). The TME comprises immune, stromal, vascular, and extracellular matrix (ECM) components, which together shape tumor growth, invasion, immune evasion, and treatment response. In GBM, tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), microglia, astrocytes, and endothelial cells interact with tumor cells through cytokine, chemokine, growth-factor, and extracellular-vesicle signaling, influencing tumor behavior and antitumor immunity. Hypoxia, vascular dysfunction, and ECM remodeling further shape this environment by altering tumor metabolism, angiogenesis, immune activity, and glioma-cell invasion. Molecular alterations, including EGFR activation, IDH mutations, BRAF alterations, and PTEN loss, also influence TME organization across glioma subtypes and contribute to differences in disease progression and treatment response. Despite advances in standard treatment, recurrence and therapeutic resistance remain major challenges, particularly in GBM. These challenges have driven interest in TME-directed strategies, including immunotherapy, anti-angiogenic therapy, metabolic interventions, vaccines, and myeloid-targeted approaches. Although several strategies have shown promise in preclinical models and clinical studies, their therapeutic efficacy remains variable. This review provides an integrated analysis of the glioma TME, with particular emphasis on GBM. We examine how immune, vascular, metabolic, ECM, and tumor-intrinsic factors interact to shape disease progression and treatment response. We also discuss emerging TME-targeted therapies and experimental models that deepen mechanistic understanding of glioma biology and may guide the development of more precise and effective treatments.

articles.title: The microbiota-gut-brain axis in ischemic stroke recovery: Mechanistic insights, evidence gaps, and translational opportunities.
articles.abstract: The microbiota-gut-brain axis has been implicated in outcome after ischemic stroke, but acute neuroprotection, later functional status, and recovery trajectories are distinct endpoints. This narrative review examines immune and metabolic mechanisms against that distinction. Experimental studies establish that sympathetic activation can initiate intestinal epithelial and mucus-barrier injury, while microbiota perturbation can alter gut-associated lymphocyte responses and their trafficking to the injured brain or meninges. Metabolite studies differ in pathway and cell-type specificity: indole-3-propionic acid has microglia-targeted triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2 evidence, indole-lactic acid has conflicting effects, and butyrate-associated interleukin-22 signaling leaves cellular sources unresolved. Human observational evidence mainly concerns later disability and cognitive impairment. Small probiotic trials report functional or cognitive signals, but mixed stroke populations, co-interventions, short follow-up, and unproven microbial mediation constrain interpretation. We assess recovery relevance separately from causal design and reporting limitations. Post-stroke experimental interventions with repeated behavioral assessments exist, but early treatment can combine tissue preservation with subsequent recovery. Clinical signals justify confirmatory studies rather than routine microbiota-directed treatment. Nutritional standardization and longitudinal biomarker validation are immediate priorities; defined interventions need reproducible exposure, safety, and rehabilitation-integrated testing. A bidirectional framework explains the evidence without equating mechanistic plausibility or preliminary clinical benefit with demonstrated neural repair.

articles.title: Polyamine metabolism in host and pathogen: Eflornithine limits Extrapulmonary Cryptococcal infection and modulates fungal virulence and macrophage responses.
articles.abstract: Cryptococcus neoformans is a leading cause of meningoencephalitis and mortality among individuals with HIV/AIDS, but therapeutic options remain limited, and the host-pathogen mechanisms underlying extrapulmonary dissemination are incompletely understood. Polyamines are metabolites produced via ornithine decarboxylase that regulate microbial virulence and host immune responses. However, their roles in both the pathogen and the host during cryptococcal infection remain unclear. Here, we investigated the potential of the clinically approved ornithine decarboxylase inhibitor α-difluoromethylornithine (DFMO; eflornithine) as a repurposed therapy for cryptococcal infection. DFMO directly inhibited the growth of C. neoformans, decreased the production of virulence factors, and enhanced the fungicidal activity of amphotericin B across cryptococcal strains. In a murine model of pulmonary C. neoformans infection, serum levels of polyamine metabolites were increased and the expression of polyamine metabolism-related genes was altered in the lung and brain. Systemic DFMO treatment reduced fungal burden in the spleen and brain but not in the lung, consistent with a role for polyamine biosynthesis in extrapulmonary spread. We further found that DFMO treatment promoted an M1-associated inflammatory phenotype in alveolar macrophages and augmented protective inflammatory responses in C. neoformans-infected mice. Treatment of C. neoformans-infected macrophages with DFMO in vitro reduced intracellular fungal growth and the expression of M2-associated genes, whereas exogenous polyamines enhanced cryptococcal invasion in a blood-brain barrier model. Collectively, these data indicate that elevated polyamine metabolites are associated with enhanced fungal virulence and altered host immunity during C. neoformans infection, and identify DFMO as a promising repurposed therapeutic candidate for disseminated cryptococcosis.

articles.title: Microglial progranulin suppresses post-ischemic tauopathy through lysosomal regulation.
articles.abstract: Post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) is a major long-term consequence of ischemic stroke. Although microglial dysfunction has been implicated in chronic neurodegeneration, the mechanisms linking microglia to post-ischemic tau pathology remain unknown. We investigated whether microglial progranulin-dependent lysosomal pathways regulate post-ischemic tau homeostasis and cognitive decline. We used rat and progranulin (Grn)-knockout mouse models of middle cerebral artery occlusion with reperfusion. Phosphorylated tau accumulation was assessed. Microglia were depleted using the colony-stimulating factor 1 receptor inhibitor PLX3397. Proteomic analyses were performed. Recombinant progranulin was administered intravenously in blinded validation experiments. Ischemic stroke induced progressive accumulation of phosphorylated tau in both neurons and microglia, whereas β-amyloid deposition was not detected. Tau burden correlated with cognitive impairment, and exogenous tau exacerbated both tau accumulation and cognitive decline. Only pre-ischemic microglial depletion accelerated tau accumulation (P = 0.041) and cognitive decline (P = 0.020), whereas delayed depletion had no effect, indicating a temporally restricted protective role of microglia. Proteomic analyses identified progranulin as a prominently downregulated protein following microglial depletion. Progranulin deficiency increased tau accumulation and reduced lysosomal marker expression, whereas recombinant progranulin reduced tau levels and improved cognitive function (P < 0.001 and P < 0.05, respectively). In conclusion, microglia exert a temporally restricted protective role by maintaining post-ischemic tau homeostasis through progranulin-dependent lysosomal function. These findings identify the microglial progranulin-lysosomal pathway as a potential therapeutic target for PSCI.

articles.title: Morphology, Histopathology, and Treatments in Cutaneous Spectrum of Yao Syndrome: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Yao syndrome (YAOS) is an adult-onset autoinflammatory disorder driven by NOD2 variants in which cutaneous manifestations occur in approximately 86% to 100% of patients and are often the earliest disease feature. The dermatologic phenotype remains poorly defined, leading to frequent misdiagnosis as chronic urticaria, atopic dermatitis, or granulomatous dermatoses.
OBJECTIVE: To characterize the cutaneous morphology, histopathology, and treatment response in genetically confirmed YAOS and to identify patterns supporting earlier dermatologic recognition.
EVIDENCE REVIEW: PubMed, MEDLINE (Ovid), Embase, and Web of Science were searched from inception through November 26, 2025. Studies with original patient-level data from individuals with genetically confirmed YAOS and at least 1 cutaneous or mucocutaneous manifestation were included; review articles, commentaries, and conference abstracts were excluded. Two reviewers independently extracted data and assessed risk of bias using Joanna Briggs Institute tools. Cutaneous findings were reclassified post hoc by a dermatologist into predefined morphologic categories. Heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis; data were synthesized narratively.
FINDINGS: Thirty-two studies encompassing 470 patients (mean [SD] age, 31.1 [5.6] years at symptom onset and 40.1 [5.0] years at diagnosis) were included. Of 470 patients, 356 (75.7%) were female, and the weighted mean diagnostic delay was 9.18 years (weighted SD of study-level means, 3.66 years). NOD2 IVS8 + 158 (JW1) is commonly identified in the disease, and individual patients often carry 2 NOD2 variants, with IVS8 + 158 (JW1) being 1 of them-it was present in 205 of 265 genotyped patients (77.4%). Primary dermatologic descriptions were nonspecific in 367 of 461 patients (79.6%). Among classifiable morphologies, urticarial-spectrum lesions were most common (143 of 171 patients [83.6%]), followed by dermatitic or eczematous lesions (20 of 171 patients [11.7%]), with rare presentations including vascular, folliculitislike, and acneiform lesions (each <1%). Histopathology demonstrated spongiotic (17 of 52 patients [32.7%]), perivascular dermatitis (15 of 52 patients [28.8%]), and granulomatous dermatitis (7 of 52 patients [13.5%]). Sicca symptoms (254 of 461 patients [55.1%]), oral ulcers (152 of 461 patients [33.0%]), arthralgia (393 of 461 patients [85.2%]), fever (323 of 461 patients [70.1%]), gastrointestinal tract symptoms (323 of 461 [70.1%]), and elevated inflammatory markers (21 of 35 patients [60.0%]) were frequent. Glucocorticoids showed the highest overall response rate (47 of 56 patients [83.9%]), followed by interleukin-1 inhibitors (63 of 101 patients [62.4%]). Sulfasalazine demonstrated moderate efficacy (34 of 70 patients [48.6%]), whereas tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α inhibitors (11 of 34 patients [32.4%]), hydroxychloroquine (6 of 21 patients [28.6%]), and methotrexate (2 of 11 patients [18.2%]) showed limited benefit.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This systematic review found that despite heterogeneous and often misclassified descriptions in the existing literature, YAOS produces a recognizable cutaneous phenotype characterized primarily by urticarial-spectrum lesions, with eczematous eruptions representing a smaller subset. Recurrent inflammatory skin eruptions accompanied by episodic systemic symptoms and refractoriness to conventional therapies should prompt NOD2 genetic testing, including intronic variant coverage.

articles.title: VP3.15 Ameliorates Tramadol Withdrawal-Associated Neurobehavioral and Neurochemical Alterations: Potential Involvement of CREB-Mediated Signaling.
articles.abstract: Opioid withdrawal is associated with neurobehavioral and biochemical alterations, including oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and disrupted neurotransmission. Tramadol is a widely used centrally acting analgesic; however, the neurobiological alterations associated with its withdrawal remain incompletely understood. The present study investigated the effects of VP3.15, a small heterocyclic molecule previously characterized as a dual GSK-3β/PDE7 inhibitor, on behavioral, oxidative, inflammatory, and neurochemical alterations associated with tramadol withdrawal in mice. A total of 100 male Swiss albino mice were randomly allocated into ten experimental groups (n = 10/group). Animals assigned to the tramadol-withdrawal groups received tramadol (50 mg/kg, s.c.) twice daily for 56 days, followed by a single tramadol dose on Day 57. Two hours later, naloxone (5 mg/kg, i.p.) was administered to precipitate withdrawal. VP3.15 (5, 10, or 20 mg/kg, i.p.) was administered once daily from Day 40 to Day 57, as a delayed intervention during prolonged tramadol exposure. Withdrawal-associated behavioral responses, including jumping frequency, withdrawal severity score, and hyperalgesia, were assessed together with brain levels of TBARS, GSH, glutamate, dopamine, serotonin, NF-κB, TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6. VP3.15 dose-dependently attenuated withdrawal-associated behavioral abnormalities, reduced lipid peroxidation, improved antioxidant status, ameliorated alterations in neurotransmitter levels, and decreased NF-κB and pro-inflammatory cytokine levels. Co-administration of 666 - 15 (10 mg/kg, i.p.), an inhibitor of CREB-mediated transcription, significantly attenuated several beneficial effects of VP3.15, suggesting a possible contribution of CREB-sensitive transcriptional processes. Clonidine (0.1 mg/kg, i.p.) also produced protective effects. Collectively, these findings demonstrate the beneficial pharmacological effects of VP3.15 against multiple alterations associated with tramadol withdrawal. Although the attenuation of these effects by 666 - 15 suggests potential involvement of CREB-sensitive processes, direct molecular engagement of CREB, GSK-3β, PDE7, and functional CREB-NF-κB interactions remains to be established.

articles.title: Inflammation in Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease: From Biomarkers and Imaging to the Limits of Anti-Inflammatory Therapy.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF THE REVIEW: Inflammation in atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease has evolved from a biological concept to a recognized determinant of cardiovascular outcomes. Nevertheless, a substantial gap remains between current evidence and its translation into routine practice. This report summarizes the evolving role of inflammation in cardiovascular risk stratification and management, from biomarkers and cardiovascular imaging to the potential and limitations of current and emerging anti-inflammatory therapies.
RECENT FINDINGS: High-sensitivity C-reactive protein has emerged as a useful biomarker to identify the residual inflammatory risk in both individuals with diagnosed atherosclerosis and in those without standard modifiable cardiovascular risk factors. Low-grade systemic inflammation may be influenced by multiple cardiometabolic and emerging risk factors and has been associated with accelerated atherosclerotic disease progression. In addition, advances in cardiovascular imaging have improved direct assessment of local vascular inflammation and its association with plaque vulnerability. Inflammation is a key contributor to the development and progression of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. However, recent neutral results from large outcome trials targeting the interleukin-6 pathway highlight the complexity and heterogeneity of the underlying mechanisms and the challenges of identifying safe and effective therapies. Inflammation should therefore not be treated as a single therapeutic entity, since clinical benefit may depend on the specific pathway targeted, the patient population selected, and the timing of intervention.

articles.title: Neuron-tumor network integration drives glioma progression through synaptic coupling, metabolic reprogramming, and neuroimmune remodeling.
articles.abstract: Traditionally regarded as space-occupying lesions, gliomas, particularly glioblastoma, are increasingly recognized as tumors that interact extensively with surrounding neural circuits. Glioma cells establish functional excitatory synapses with neurons and form interconnected networks through tumor microtubes, facilitating electrical integration and intercellular communication. They also coopt activity-dependent neuronal paracrine factors to promote proliferation and exploit neurotransmitter signaling and ion channels to sustain a hyperexcitable tumor microenvironment. Beyond neuronal signaling, gliomas engage in metabolic interactions with surrounding cells, including astrocyte-to-glioma mitochondrial transfer, macrophage-mediated recycling of myelin-derived lipids, and tumor-induced astrocyte reprogramming. These processes are closely associated with immunosuppressive signaling. Together, these mechanisms may establish self-reinforcing neuron-tumor feedback loops that remodel neural circuits and contribute to epilepsy, cognitive decline, and therapeutic resistance in patients. This review synthesizes current evidence across 4 interconnected dimensions: physical connectivity, chemical signaling hijacking, metabolic reprogramming, and neuroimmune remodeling. Building on these findings, we propose a hypothesis-generating model linking neural network integration, altered metabolic resource exchange, and immunosuppressive niches. The model distinguishes experimentally supported findings from proposed feedback relationships, identifies testable predictions, and provides a rationale for organizing network-oriented therapeutic strategies according to the tumor-host interactions they target while considering the preservation of normal brain function.

articles.title: Cardiomyocyte-derived circulating extracellular vesicles enable a non-invasive liquid biopsy of human myocardium.
articles.abstract: Non-invasive interrogation of difficult-to-sample tissues remains a central challenge in human health. Here, we identify and characterize cardiomyocyte-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs; "cardiovesicles") as a liquid interface to the myocardium. Integrating induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes, genetic models, and multi-omics, we identify two cardiomyocyte-enriched surface markers (POPDC2 and CHRNE), enabling antibody-based cardiovesicle immunocapture from human plasma. Cardiovesicles are enriched for cardiomyocyte transcripts, exhibiting disease-specific transcriptional signatures in heart failure and myocardial infarction. Paired human myocardial tissue-plasma analyses demonstrate cardiac enrichment (versus bulk EVs) and concordance with myocardial single-nucleus transcriptional profiles. In patients undergoing cardiopulmonary bypass, cardiovesicles capture rapid, dynamic transcriptional changes that parallel cardiomyocyte (not fibroblast, endothelial, and myeloid) responses to ischemic stress. Functional genomics implicates cardiovesicle transcripts in cardiomyocyte cell-specific cardiovascular disease liability in large human populations. Cardiovesicles may capture dynamic cardiomyocyte states in humans that reflect genetic disease liability, supporting an EV-based approach to non-invasive liquid biopsy of the myocardium.

articles.title: Pathology-adapted peptide-oligonucleotide nanohybrid mitigates glucocorticoid-induced bone loss.
articles.abstract: Glucocorticoid-induced bone loss (GIBL) remains a major clinical challenge, manifested by both systemic osteopenia and osteonecrosis of the femoral head under chronic glucocorticoid exposure, yet current therapies are limited in coordinately addressing bone deterioration and vascular impairment. With advances in precision medicine, oligonucleotide therapeutics offer opportunities for pathophysiology-informed intervention. Here, we report a pathology-adapted peptide-oligonucleotide nanohybrid (PON) developed for targeted miR-26a-5p delivery to glucocorticoid-injured bone. By integrating self-assembly, bone targeting, enzyme responsiveness, cell penetration, and lysosomal escape, PONs were designed to incorporate pathology-responsive delivery features and address key barriers to oligonucleotide delivery. Mechanistically, PON-mediated miR-26a-5p delivery reduced GSK-3β expression and promoted HIF-1α stabilization, thereby preserving osteogenesis-angiogenesis coupling and attenuating apoptosis. In a rat model of GIBL, systemic PON administration protects against early skeletal and vascular injury and limits progression after disease establishment. These findings identify the therapeutic relevance of miR-26a-5p in GIBL, and support the potential of PON system for bone-targeted oligonucleotide therapy.

articles.title: Smooth muscle DDIT4 exacerbates vascular remodeling in atherosclerosis and vascular injury by impairing PDC activity.
articles.abstract: Restenosis and atherosclerosis remain therapeutic challenges. Vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) phenotypic switching is a central driver. DNA damage inducible transcript 4 (DDIT4) is implicated in vascular disease, but its role in restenosis and atherosclerosis is unknown. Here we show that DDIT4 is markedly increased in PDGF-BB- or IL-1β-stimulated dedifferentiated VSMCs and reduced in differentiated VSMCs. DDIT4 is upregulated in VSMCs within neointima and atherosclerotic lesions of mice and humans, correlating with disease progression. DDIT4 overexpression promotes VSMC proliferation and phenotypic switching, whereas knockdown suppresses these effects. AAV9-mediated Ddit4 overexpression exacerbates neointimal hyperplasia in atherosclerosis and vascular injury models, while VSMC-specific Ddit4 deletion attenuates it. DDIT4 binds the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex, destabilizing subunit interactions and impairing activity. Resulting acetyl-CoA decline reduces histone acetylation, especially at contractile gene promoters, diminishing H3K9/H3K27 acetylation and chromatin accessibility, thereby repressing contractile genes. Targeting DDIT4 is a promising therapeutic strategy for restenosis and atherosclerosis.
